p0: P0 define the exact broker-committed output delivery path (§4.10(g)). rev-29's renderer<->broker reply frame carried only {protocol, status, conversation_id, reason?} — insufficient for the renderer to obtain the exact verified+persisted message. rev-30 locks ONE model: brops.renderer-governed-turn-result.v1 returns the broker-produced immutable UI projection message{message_id, role:assistant, author, body, created_at_ms, trust_state:trusted_verified} on commit (NO message on blocked; a CLOSED reason enum). The returned body is the exact strict-UTF8 bytes whose length+SHA-256 matched the signed accepted-output envelope; message_id/body/trust_state equal the row the broker verification tx committed (in-tx re-read; any mismatch => fail-closed commit_readback_mismatch); ONLY the broker tx creates the verified message + trust_state; the renderer never reads/writes the trust DB and no renderer command (incl. generic chat writes) can create/edit/mark it; output-bytes == persisted body == returned body is equality-tested; forged renderer events can never render Verified; blocked turns return no assistant message. +positive/negative E2E delivery tests.
p1: P1-1 add exact IPC request correlation + payload-aware idempotency. A NON-authoritative client_request_id (UUIDv4) on the request grants no signing/verification authority; the broker mints its OWN authoritative broker_turn_id + request_nonce. Idempotency is keyed on the exact normalized {client_request_id, conversation_id, agent}: identical live duplicate => reattach to the same broker_turn_id; same client_request_id with a different conversation or agent => retry_conflict; a different request while the conversation already has a live turn => explicit turn_in_progress (NOT silent reattachment — replaces the old 'idempotent on conversation_id' rule); every reply echoes client_request_id + broker_turn_id; a late reply from an earlier timed-out request cannot satisfy a newer request. +disconnect/reconnect/duplicate/conflicting-agent/late-reply tests.

P1-2 complete the stdin/stdout/stderr (FDs 0/1/2) lifecycle (§2.7). The recorder OPENS controlled inert endpoints for 0/1/2, then maps + clears FD_CLOEXEC on 3-6, then launches the helper. The launcher verifies 0/1/2 are exactly the approved inert endpoints, rejects interactive/inherited/unexpected stdio, closes 0/1/2 or sets FD_CLOEXEC on them BEFORE fexecve, and confirms ONLY 3-6 survive into the executor. +a real executor test that enumerates /proc/self/fd and proves only FDs 3-6 are inherited.
